title: Completed pullback
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes, with its morphism of small pro-etale topoi and inverse image $g^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use the Noetherian adic datum $A,I,P_n=A/I^n$, completed coefficient sheaves $A_W=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_W$, and strict tower categories $\operatorname{Tow}_A(W)$, for $W=T,T'$, of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Define the coefficient structure map
$$c_g:g^{-1}A_T\longrightarrow A_{T'}$$
by its components $g^{-1}A_T\to g^{-1}(P_n)_T\to(P_n)_{T'}$; they are compatible with quotient maps and hence give a map into the inverse limit. Module pullback along $c_g$ is $g^*M=g^{-1}M\otimes_{g^{-1}A_T}A_{T'}$. At finite level write $g_n^*$ for the module inverse image over the constant sheaves $(P_n)_T,(P_n)_{T'}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The map $c_g$ is a structure map, without an assumption that it is an isomorphism.

On complexes of strict towers, apply module pullback levelwise. Define its total left derived functor
$$Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}:D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))\longrightarrow D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T'))$$
using the objectwise K-flat resolving class of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements], with $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the resolving-class construction of [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. Thus a strict replacement $P_\bullet\to M_\bullet$ from that class gives the representative $g^*P_\bullet$; the transition maps are the images under $g^*$ of the transition maps of $P_\bullet$.

For the reduction tower $K_\bullet$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], its $n$-th evaluation is canonically $Lg_n^*K_n$, regarded as an $A_{T'}$-complex by restriction along $A_{T'}\to(P_n)_{T'}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. The coefficient comparison used here is the flat constant-to-completed comparison and its finite reductions in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]; finite constant-coefficient pullback is exact [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact].

For $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ derived $I$-complete in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], define
$$Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K=\operatorname{Rlim}\bigl(Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet\bigr)\quad\text{in }D(T'_{\mathrm{proet}},A),$$
where $\operatorname{Rlim}$ is [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit]. Ordinary $Lg^*K$ is computed by the same K-flat class with the one-object indexing category. Write $\Delta$ for the constant strict tower functor. The quotient maps give a strict morphism $\Delta QK\to(QK\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T)_n$, where $QK$ is the K-flat representative with flat terms. Applying $Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}$ gives a morphism $\Delta Lg^*K\to Lg^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}K_\bullet$, since the constant tower on $QK$ is already in the resolving class. Use the functor $\operatorname{Rlim}$ of [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality]. The canonical map from a complex $C$ to $\operatorname{Rlim}\Delta C$ is obtained by taking a tower K-injective resolution $\Delta C\to I_\bullet$ and factoring its compatible component maps $C\to I_n$ through $\varprojlim I_n$. Compose this map for $C=Lg^*K$ with $\operatorname{Rlim}$ of the strict-tower morphism just constructed. This defines the comparison $Lg^*K\to Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ without selecting a cone map from unrelated morphisms in a triangulated category. Its component maps are the images of the finite quotient maps.

Under restriction to constant coefficients and the equivalences of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], this is the completed pullback $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ of Stacks Tag 099N (proetale-lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case), clauses (2) and (5): ordinary pullback followed by derived completion, equivalently $R\lim_n Lg^*(K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T)$. Here [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] identifies intrinsic Koszul completeness with the local Stacks condition, and its natural finite-reduction isomorphisms identify the pulled-back tower with the finite-reduction tower of constant-coefficient pullback, including transition maps. The same lemma identifies derived limits and completion units under restriction of scalars. Thus the displayed derived limit is ordinary pullback followed by derived completion, and the comparison just constructed is its completion unit. This comparison is on derived-complete categories under the coefficient equivalences, with the ambient categories of constant and completed coefficient modules distinguished.

proof.text: For the strict completed-coefficient interface in Sheaf.Paper.CompletedPullback, exactness of towerModulePull follows from exactness of the ringed module inverse image and the pointwise finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation instances for whiskering right. Construct each finite-preservation structure from the instances for every finite shape. All completed pullback definitions are retained.

For each generating list and each representative, use the unit-compatible Koszul-to-quotient isomorphism. The intrinsic unit is invertible if and only if its composite with that isomorphism is invertible, namely the canonical quotient unit. This proves the forward implication uniformly. For the converse choose a finite generating family using ideal finite generation and choose the canonical localization representative of K. Apply the reverse invertibility implication to that family and representative. This proves towerComplete_iff_intrinsic without changing either completeness definition.

For $g:Y'\to Y$ define

$$
Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K:=
R\varprojlim_n\bigl(Lg^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda\Lambda/I^n\bigr).
$$

The comparison from ordinary pullback is the completion map of $Lg^*K$.

split_report.summary: Split this definition into its explicit ringed coefficient map, strict-diagram derived pullback construction, finite-level interpretation, and derived limit. Added two general statement-only bridge lemmas for diagram K-flat replacements and constant-to-completed coefficients; reused the existing resolving-class theorem and finite-level exactness. Removed the unused duplicate complete-coefficient datum dependency and named intrinsic completeness explicitly. No proof steps are added to a definition. Repair: the Rlim comparison is constructed by the existing functoriality theorem from a constant-tower morphism, and the final Stacks identification explicitly tracks natural finite pullback, transition maps, coefficient equivalence, and completion units.
